analysis.investment_thesis: KEC International is a competent EPC contractor with a 80-year track record, growing revenues from INR 8,518 Cr to INR 21,847 Cr — but EPC businesses with 6.3% operating margins, D/E of 0.94, and finance costs of INR 839 Cr eating nearly half of operating income are not the kind of durable, high-return franchises I seek. The forward P/E of 14.83x suggests modest value but insufficient margin of safety for the risks.
key_strengths: Diversified EPC franchise across T&D, railways, solar, cables, and civil — reduces single-segment concentration risk
Revenue compounding at 11% over 9 years with a strong FY25 recovery in net profit to INR 571 Cr after the FY23 trough of INR 176 Cr
ROCE of 18% is creditable for an EPC business; RPG group promoter with 50.1% stake provides strategic stability
key_risks: Debt/equity of 0.94 with INR 839 Cr finance costs vs INR 1,683 Cr operating income — interest burden consumes 50% of operating profit, leaving little room for error
EPC margins are structurally thin (6.33% operating) with high working capital intensity; a project delay or commodity cost spike can wipe out profits, as FY22-23 demonstrated (profit fell 68%)
Free cash flow is highly volatile: -INR 425 Cr (FY22), +INR 451 Cr (FY23), +INR 78 Cr (FY24), +INR 270 Cr (FY25) — poor visibility for long-term owners
red_flags: Borrowings have surged from INR 2,066 Cr (FY21) to INR 5,308 Cr (FY25) — debt is growing faster than equity
Net profit of INR 571 Cr on revenue of INR 21,847 Cr implies a net margin of just 2.6% — this is not a durable competitive advantage, it is a thin spread on large volumes
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KEC operates in critical Indian infrastructure — power transmission, railways, solar — all of which have genuine government-driven demand. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 11% is respectable, and the FY25 recovery in both margins and profits is encouraging after the FY22-23 commodity-driven pain. The cables segment adds modest recurring character to an otherwise lumpy order-book business.

But EPC companies live and die by execution on large, fixed-price contracts. The structural 6.3% operating margin and 2.6% net margin leave almost no cushion. With D/E near 1.0 and interest costs at INR 839 Cr, a bad project or a credit tightening cycle could be painful. This is not a business I'd want to own in a downturn — I need businesses that get stronger when times are hard, not ones that get squeezed. At 21x P/E and these characteristics, I'd watch but not buy.
